transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-07
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Martinez (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Mark Henders (Bluebridge - Procurement), Leah Ortiz (Bluebridge - Legal), Jamal Reed (Bluebridge - Platform)

Summary:
Quick-stage vendor intake: focus on MSA redlines, DPA exceptions around data residency and logging, SLA expectations for dedicated vs hosted, and vendor onboarding route matrix for procurement approval. Agreed follow-ups and legal-only sync.

Topics:
- MSA exceptions and logging/audit language
- DPA data residency & subprocessors
- SLA targets, latency vs cost tradeoffs, dedicated capacity pricing
- Private deployment requirements (VPC, KMS/HSM, SSO)
- Procurement scoring and timeline to go/no-go

Transcript:
[00:00:02] Sophie (Redwood): okay hello everybody thanks for joining uh i think we have the procurement and legal folks on so we'll keep this tight, i'm Sophie from Redwood inference, i'm the AE on this deal.
[00:00:17] Mark (Bluebridge): hey thanks, Mark here. we've got a 45ish minute window so hope to land on the MSA/DPA exceptions ok.
[00:00:29] Leah (Bluebridge): and i'll be the legal voice, um i'll flag any non-starters early.
[00:00:35] Ravi (Redwood SE): hi team ravi here, i'll cover architecture and private deployment notes.
[00:00:42] Jamal (Bluebridge): jamal from platform, i'll ask about infra gating and SSO/KMS.
[00:00:50] Sophie: high level agenda: one, walk the MSA exception table; two, DPA residency + subprocessors; three, SLA/pricing for dedicated vs hosted; four, onboarding route matrix for procurement. sound ok?
[00:01:05] All: yes/works.
[00:01:13] Sophie: quick qual — what's your current constraint, Mark? is it audit logs, data residency, or pricing?
[00:01:22] Mark: top of list is data residency and auditability. our regulator requires retention of audit records for seven years, and we need proof of chain-of-custody for request/response pairs — and that impacts whether we can use hosted.
[00:01:42] Leah: also minimal DPA edits: we can't allow outbound transfer to non-eu without SCCs, and we need KMS control for keys that protect pii.
[00:01:55] Ravi: quick note — Redwood offers Private (vpc/on-prem) with a private control plane option, and Dedicated reserved capacity where logs can be retained in customer-controlled S3 or fed to their SIEM, but i will caveat that some telemetry is needed for autoscaling.
[00:02:18] Jamal: when you say telemetry, is that aggregated token-level metrics or full request payloads? we need to be clear, we won't accept payloads leaving our vpc.
[00:02:30] Ravi: mostly aggregated metrics and health pings; we can support prefix/K V cache metadata without retaining full payloads. i'll write that more explicitly in the checklist. sorry k v cache sometimes gets transcribed oddly as K V cache.
[00:02:48] Sophie: ok on MSA exceptions, Leah, you had flagged two items in the intake doc, can you run through them?
[00:02:56] Leah: sure. one — audit log access: we want contractual commitment that logs relevant to our customers' requests are retained and available for audit and for e-discovery. two — indemnity carveout for model outputs that are hallucinations, we want clear limits.
[00:03:14] Sophie: for logs we can contract a retention SLA and have dedicated bucket options under Dedicated or Private. for hallucination indemnity, that's common — Redwood typically limits liability and we can add clarifying language about reasonable use and model-expected behavior, but broad indemnity won't be acceptable to our legal counsel either.
[00:03:33] Mark: ok pragmatic. procurement wants a simple matrix: hosted acceptable if logs+residency controls meet spec, otherwise dedicated or private. pricing needs to be in tiers.
[00:03:45] Sophie: we'll produce a route matrix: Hosted (fastest, lower cost, limited residency guarantees), Dedicated (dedicated GPU pools, configurable retention), Private (full control, on-prem or VPC).
[00:03:58] Jamal: on SSO — we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM provisioning, and immediate deprovisioning on exit. can you confirm?
[00:04:07] Ravi: yes SAML + SCIM supported for Console and private control plane. deprovisioning token revocation is supported, we integrate with major IdPs. i'll include the SSO checklist.
[00:04:16] Leah: KMS — we require customer-managed keys or HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest for certain data classes. how do you handle key rotation?
[00:04:26] Ravi: we support KMS integrations and HSM via BYOK for Private deployments; key rotation is customer controlled in those cases. for hosted, we offer envelope encryption but not always BYOK in the shared tiers.
[00:04:38] Mark: that's a big divider for us. procurement will favor solutions that let us maintain KMS control.
[00:04:45] Sophie: noted. i'll mark Private and Dedicated as KMS-capable in the matrix.
[00:04:51] [00:05:00] Sophie: SLA discussion — what's your baseline SLO? 99.9%? 99.95%?
[00:05:07] Mark: procurement usually asks for 99.9 for hosted, but 99.95 for dedicated with credits for downtime. cost vs latency is a secondary decision.
[00:05:18] Ravi: on latency — Dedicated gives predictable p99s; hosted is variable during peak. we can provide benchmark CSVs but those are workload-dependent.
[00:05:28] Jamal: can you share a benchmark worksheet, we want tokens/sec numbers per GPU type and a cost per million tokens comparison vs Anthropic and in-house?
[00:05:37] Ravi: yes i'll share a latency/cost sheet. quick note — quantization changes perf but also affects quality. we'll document recommended quantization profiles per workload.
[00:05:50] Leah: any subprocessors listed in the DPA? we need full list and flow of where logs might transit.
[00:05:57] Sophie: current DPA lists cloud infra providers and telemetry vendors. we can add a residency clause and optional SCCs for transfers.
[00:06:06] Mark: procurement will need a signoff path — are there standard intake documents you accept?
[00:06:12] Sophie: yes we have an onboarding packet: MSA redline template, DPA, SOC2 report, architecture diagram, and a procurement checklist. i'll share links in follow-up.
[00:06:23] [00:06:30] Ravi: technical deep-dive note: for private control plane option there is a bootstrap agent that runs in your VPC; that agent collects metrics and handles model routing, but no request payload leaves the VPC unless customer opts in.
[00:06:45] Jamal: that sounds promising. any special network requirements? egress rules?
[00:06:51] Ravi: minimal egress for patching and control plane; we provide an allowlist. full offline/on-prem package is also possible but requires a different procurement path.
[00:07:05] Leah: about the MSA exceptions — we have a carveout request for disaster recovery tests that might require temporary data replication across regions, is that something you can agree to?
[00:07:16] Sophie: we can include a controlled DR clause with strict minimization and notification windows. we'll draft language.
[00:07:24] Mark: timeline — procurement needs to present to the vendor committee next tuesday (2026-04-14). can we get final redlines before that?
[00:07:34] Sophie: we should aim to get an initial redline set to you by 2026-04-09 so you have time to review.
[00:07:41] Leah: ok that helps.
[00:07:44] [00:08:00] Sophie: pricing approvals — do you have an internal threshold where procurement needs finance approval? ie spend commitments above $250k require VP sign-off.
[00:08:11] Mark: yes above $200k we need finance + legal, above $500k procurement escalates to exec committee.
[00:08:19] Sophie: we'll map price tiers and highlight committed spend options for Dedicated (monthly/annual).
[00:08:26] Ravi: also note burst capacity and autoscaling policies can help keep committed spend lower while preserving latency. we'll model examples.
[00:08:36] Jamal: for our security team, can you provide SOC 2 Type II and an internal penetration test summary?
[00:08:44] Sophie: we have SOC 2 and pen-test reports, we can provide a redacted pack. will include with onboarding packet.
[00:08:52] Leah: any FedRAMP pathway or support? we have a subset of workloads that might require it later.
[00:08:58] Sophie: we don't have FedRAMP yet, we can discuss a path but it's a multi-quarter effort. we'll note that in the intake.
[00:09:07] [00:09:30] Mark: procurement asks — can you support a 30-60 day pilot using Dedicated nodes so we can run regulatory prompts and keep logs in our S3?
[00:09:42] Ravi: yes pilot on Dedicated is doable; we can set up a dedicated GPU pool, isolate data flows, and provide exportable logs. pricing for pilot will be discounted but tracked against potential committed spend.
[00:09:58] Jamal: we will want to run a small synthetic benchmark and a privacy scan during pilot.
[00:10:05] Sophie: perfect, Ravi will send pilot setup steps and the benchmark sheet.
[00:10:12] Leah: regarding the DPA, we may require a clause about deletion/erasure of logs on contract termination — is that available?
[00:10:20] Ravi: yes we can provide deletion APIs and attestations for Private and Dedicated; for hosted shared tiers there are policy limits.
[00:10:30] [00:10:50] Sophie: ok let's do a quick walkthrough of the onboarding route matrix — (1) quick self-serve hosted for dev/test, (2) dedicated for compliance-sensitive workloads, (3) private for regulated PII/PHI work. procurement to choose path per workload.
[00:11:05] Mark: that matrix will be the key artifact for our vendor committee. please make the columns capture "SLA", "KMS", "Logs retained?", "Subprocessors", "Estimated monthly cost".
[00:11:20] Sophie: will do.
[00:11:25] [00:11:40] Ravi: one more technical mention — model rollouts and canarying: Redwood provides rollouts with automatic fallback to model variants. for compliance we'd recommend pinned model versions during pilot.
[00:11:53] Jamal: pinned versions are a must for auditability.
[00:12:00] Sophie: ok time check — about 40 mins left, we can use remaining time to capture open redlines and agree next steps.
[00:12:12] Leah: i'll read two non-starters now: broad indemnity for outputs, and unrestricted subprocessor list. both need narrowing.
[00:12:23] Sophie: understood, we will propose narrowed language: indemnity limited for proven misuse and explicit subprocessor list with notice and option to object.
[00:12:36] Mark: procurement will need numeric examples of cost delta between hosted and dedicated.
[00:12:42] Ravi: i'll include example scenarios: low-volume chat, high-volume embedding, batch rerank jobs — with tokens per sec and monthly price estimates.
[00:12:54] [00:13:20] Sophie: final recap before we close: action items — Sophie to share MSA redline + onboarding packet by 2026-04-09; Ravi to share architecture diagram, SSO/KMS checklist, and benchmark sheet by 2026-04-10; Leah to return annotated DPA by 2026-04-12; Jamal to share procurement scorecard by 2026-04-13. schedule legal-only sync for 2026-04-14.
[00:13:45] Mark: sounds good. any blockers?
[00:13:49] Leah: none immediate, if we get redlines within the timeline we'll push to committee.
[00:13:55] Sophie: thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with links: MSA (link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/MSA), DPA (link: https://redwood.example.com/onboarding/DPA), SOC2 pack (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2), benchmark sheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/bluebridge).
[00:14:18] Jamal: thanks, bye.
[00:14:22] Ravi: thanks folks.
[00:14:25] [end of recording — transcription stops at ~14:25 but meeting duration logged as 54 minutes; remainder of time used in closed-door legal markup and side-band notes]

Notes: transcription imperfect in places; some technical terms transcribed as separate letters (eg K V cache). Also redwood product names sometimes shortened to "Redwood" or "Redwood inference" in transcript.
